findings.claim: the first push of a new branch skipped the guard entirely (no origin/<branch> yet): the anchor fallback consulted origin/HEAD only when detached, so a branch-shape smuggle audited from the NEW base
deleting .stallion-base was exempt from the old-base audit (headBase null read as no accusation); the anchor ordering and byte-equality semantics were unpinned
the trust anchor is client-writable state: origin tracking refs and origin/HEAD are updatable in-clone, and CI checkout sets no origin/HEAD
findings.justification: remote-tracking refs are plain-trust state, the documented boundary of the plain-JSON register world; the git history of .stallion-base is the tamper evidence, and the server-pinned CI delta step re-judges existing-branch pushes.

findings.claim: a stale origin/HEAD anchors the verdict on the wrong branch; the CI --base event.before sha can never equal the old base VALUE, so a compliant move would die on runners that do set origin/HEAD
findings.justification: stale origin/HEAD is the set-head -a discipline (future doctor check); the CI shape concern is real and registered — runner-anchored verdicts defer to the server-pinned event.before range, and new-branch first pushes remain the documented boundary until task-commit binding (issue #8).
